entries.name: CHANNEL_PATTERN
entries.signature: export declare const CHANNEL_PATTERN: RegExp;
entries.jsdocSummary: A channel name: a Postgres identifier of 1 to 63 characters of `[a-z0-9_]`.

entries.name: MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES
entries.signature: export declare const MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 7999;
entries.jsdocSummary: The largest payload, in UTF-8 bytes. Postgres NOTIFY refuses 8000 bytes or more, so the limit is 7999.

entries.name: OnMessage
entries.signature: export type OnMessage = (payload: string) => void;
entries.jsdocSummary: Called once per message on the channel it was given to.

entries.name: PubSub
entries.signature: export type PubSub<SubscribeFailure = never> = { /** Sends `payload` to the channel's subscribers now. Resolves once the backend accepted it. */ publish(channel: string, payload: string): Promise<void>; /** * Resolves once the subscription is live: every later publish on `channel` reaches `onMessage`. * Resolves to `SubscribeFailure` instead when the backend cannot listen; nothing is subscribed then. */ subscribe(channel: string, onMessage: OnMessage): Promise<Unsubscribe | SubscribeFailure>; /** Stops every subscription and frees the backend's connections. Later calls throw a `closed` error. */ close(): Promise<void>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Publish and subscribe on named channels. `SubscribeFailure` is what `subscribe` returns when the backend cannot listen: `db.listen_unavailable` for pg, none (`never`) for the others.

entries.name: PUBSUB_ERROR_CODES
entries.signature: export declare const PUBSUB_ERROR_CODES: { /** * The channel is not 1 to 63 characters of `[a-z0-9_]` (a Postgres identifier). * * @fix Use a short lower-case name such as `orders_changed`. * @verify bun run test -- src/testing/memory.contract.test.ts */ readonly channel: 'ARKI_PUBSUB_E001'; /** * The payload is 8000 bytes or more in UTF-8 (NOTIFY refuses it; the limit is 7999). * * @fix Send an id and let the subscriber read the rest from the database. * @verify bun run test -- src/testing/memory.contract.test.ts */ readonly payload: 'ARKI_PUBSUB_E002'; /** * The pubsub was closed; it cannot publish or subscribe any more. * * @fix Make a new pubsub, or close it only when the app shuts down. * @verify bun run test -- src/testing/memory.contract.test.ts */ readonly closed: 'ARKI_PUBSUB_E003'; /** * Bad setup: a non-positive `intervalMs` or `retainMs`. * * @fix Fix the option named in the message. * @verify bun run test -- src/sqlite/sqlite.test.ts */ readonly config: 'ARKI_PUBSUB_E004'; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Stable ids, one per `PubSubError.code`. Never renumber.

entries.name: PubSubError
entries.signature: export declare class PubSubError extends Error { readonly code: PubSubErrorCode; /** The stable id of `code`, e.g. `ARKI_PUBSUB_E001`. */ readonly errorCode: (typeof PUBSUB_ERROR_CODES)[PubSubErrorCode]; /** What to do about it, in one sentence. */ readonly remediation: string; constructor(init: { readonly code: PubSubErrorCode; readonly message: string; readonly remediation: string; }); }
entries.jsdocSummary: A thrown, coded error of `@arki/pubsub`: a bad call or a closed pubsub.

entries.name: PubSubErrorCode
entries.signature: export type PubSubErrorCode = keyof typeof PUBSUB_ERROR_CODES;
entries.jsdocSummary: Which failure a {@link PubSubError} is.

entries.name: TransactionalPubSub
entries.signature: export type TransactionalPubSub<Tx, SubscribeFailure = never> = PubSub<SubscribeFailure> & { /** Sent when `tx` commits; dropped if it rolls back. */ publishIn(tx: Tx, channel: string, payload: string): Promise<void>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A {@link PubSub} that can also publish inside the writer's own database transaction.

entries.name: Unsubscribe
entries.signature: export type Unsubscribe = () => Promise<void>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Stops one subscription. Calling it again does nothing. Its shape fits `@arki/journal`'s `WakeListener`, so `listen: fn => pubsub.subscribe(channel, fn)` needs no adapter (a subscribe failure fits it too: the worker's `start()` returns it).

entries.name: memoryPubSub
entries.signature: export declare function memoryPubSub(): PubSub;
entries.jsdocSummary: A pubsub inside this process. Each call makes its own, separate bus. Messages arrive on a later microtask, never inside `publish`, in the order they were published.

entries.name: pgPubSub
entries.signature: export declare function pgPubSub(options: PgPubSubOptions): TransactionalPubSub<PgTransaction, ReturnType<typeof ListenUnavailable>>;
entries.jsdocSummary: A pubsub over Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY. `subscribe` resolves to `db.listen_unavailable` (`ListenUnavailable` from `@arki/db/pg`) when the channel's first connection or `LISTEN` fails.

entries.name: PgPubSubOptions
entries.signature: export type PgPubSubOptions = { /** A session pool on the direct host, never a transaction pooler. Not closed by `close()`. */ readonly pool: PgPubSubPool; /** Reconnect and health-check timing of the listen clients. */ readonly listen?: ListenOptions; };

entries.name: PgPubSubPool
entries.signature: export type PgPubSubPool = ListenPool & { query(text: string, values: unknown[]): Promise<unknown>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A `pg` pool (`new pg.Pool(...)`, or a Drizzle node-postgres database's `$client`): it hands out listen clients and runs `pg_notify`.

entries.name: PgTransaction
entries.signature: export type PgTransaction = PgAsyncTransaction<PgQueryResultHKT, AnyRelations>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Any Drizzle Postgres transaction (node-postgres, postgres.js, PGlite, …).

entries.name: redisPubSub
entries.signature: export declare function redisPubSub(options: RedisPubSubOptions): PubSub;
entries.jsdocSummary: A pubsub over Redis pub/sub.

entries.name: RedisPubSubOptions
entries.signature: export type RedisPubSubOptions = { /** An ioredis client. It publishes; a duplicate of it subscribes. `close()` closes only the duplicate. */ readonly client: Redis; };

entries.name: pubsubTable
entries.signature: export declare function pubsubTable(name?: string): import("drizzle-orm/sqlite-core").SQLiteTableWithColumns<{ name: string; schema: undefined; columns: { id: import("drizzle-orm/sqlite-core").SQLiteColumn<{ name: string; tableName: string; dataType: "number int53"; data: number; driverParam: number; notNull: true; hasDefault: true; isPrimaryKey: true; isAutoincrement: false; hasRuntimeDefault: false; enumValues: undefined; baseColumn: never; identity: undefined; generated: undefined; }, {}>; channel: import("drizzle-orm/sqlite-core").SQLiteColumn<{ name: string; tableName: string; dataType: "string"; data: string; driverParam: string; notNull: true; hasDefault: false; isPrimaryKey: false; isAutoincrement: false; hasRuntimeDefault: false; enumValues: [string, ...string[]]; baseColumn: never; identity: undefined; generated: undefined; }, {}>; payload: import("drizzle-orm/sqlite-core").SQLiteColumn<{ name: string; tableName: string; dataType: "string"; data: string; driverParam: string; notNull: true; hasDefault: false; isPrimaryKey: false; isAutoincrement: false; hasRuntimeDefault: false; enumValues: [string, ...string[]]; baseColumn: never; identity: undefined; generated: undefined; }, {}>; createdAt: import("drizzle-orm/sqlite-core").SQLiteColumn<{ name: string; tableName: string; dataType: "object date"; data: Date; driverParam: number; notNull: true; hasDefault: true; isPrimaryKey: false; isAutoincrement: false; hasRuntimeDefault: false; enumValues: undefined; baseColumn: never; identity: undefined; generated: undefined; }, {}>; }; dialect: 'sqlite'; }>;
entries.jsdocSummary: The messages table: `id` (auto-increment, the subscribers' cursor), `channel`, `payload` and `createdAt` (the database clock, used for retention). Export it from your schema so your migrations create it.

entries.name: PubsubTable
entries.signature: export type PubsubTable = ReturnType<typeof pubsubTable>;
entries.jsdocSummary: The table {@link pubsubTable} builds.

entries.name: sqlitePubSub
entries.signature: export declare function sqlitePubSub<TDb extends SqlitePubSubDb>(options: SqlitePubSubOptions<TDb>): TransactionalPubSub<TransactionOf<TDb>>;
entries.jsdocSummary: A pubsub over a SQLite message table. Each subscriber starts at the newest row when it subscribes; one loop per pubsub reads `id > cursor` for the subscribed channels every `intervalMs`. `publishIn(tx, …)` inserts the row in your transaction: it is seen at commit and never if the transaction rolls back. SQLite has one writer, so ids commit in order and no row is skipped.

entries.name: SqlitePubSubDb
entries.signature: export type SqlitePubSubDb = SQLiteAsyncDatabase<'async', unknown, AnyRelations>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Any async Drizzle SQLite database or transaction; libSQL is the one `@arki/db` supports.

entries.name: SqlitePubSubOptions
entries.signature: export type SqlitePubSubOptions<TDb> = { /** The Drizzle database the table lives in. Subscribers read through it; `publish` writes through it. */ readonly db: TDb; /** The table from `pubsubTable()`. Default: `pubsubTable()`, named `arki_pubsub`. */ readonly table?: PubsubTable; /** How often subscribers read new rows, in milliseconds. Default 250. */ readonly intervalMs?: number; /** Rows older than this many milliseconds are deleted by the next publisher. Default 60000. */ readonly retainMs?: number; };

entries.name: describePubSubContract
entries.signature: export declare function describePubSubContract<Tx>(name: string, make: () => Promise<PubSubSubject | TransactionalPubSubSubject<Tx>>, options?: PubSubContractOptions): void;
entries.jsdocSummary: Register the conformance cases with vitest. `make` returns a fresh pubsub per case; return `{ pubsub, transaction }` for a backend with `publishIn` to run the transaction cases too.

entries.name: PubSubContractOptions
entries.signature: export type PubSubContractOptions = { /** How long to wait before saying nothing arrived. Default 150 ms; a polling backend needs a few intervals. */ readonly settleMs?: number; /** How long to wait for a message that must arrive. Default 5000 ms. */ readonly timeoutMs?: number; /** True when two `make()` results share one transport (a database or a server), so one hears the other. Default true. */ readonly shared?: boolean; };

entries.name: PubSubSubject
entries.signature: export type PubSubSubject = { readonly pubsub: PubSub; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A fresh pubsub for one case. The suite closes it.

entries.name: TransactionalPubSubSubject
entries.signature: export type TransactionalPubSubSubject<Tx> = { readonly pubsub: TransactionalPubSub<Tx>; /** Runs `fn` in one transaction: commits when it resolves, rolls back when it throws. Usually `fn => db.transaction(fn)`. */ readonly transaction: (fn: (tx: Tx) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A fresh transactional pubsub for one case, with a way to open a transaction it can publish in.
